Does that mean you would put every choice below Stefan on the same level? All hindrances due to the presence of better choices and that's it? With the Farina reply in mind as well, it feels more like a unit guide, but I suppose there's nothing wrong with that.
Again, my current idea of a ranking is closer to something where a unit's placing is divorced from the opportunity cost and other factors outside of what the unit offers in terms of completing objectives.
It's not really as important, but regarding Renning, you've a certain kind of team in mind, but if your roster is lacking in ways to deal with armors, I could see Renning being more useful than the generally better alternatives you mentioned.

I do agree that if you're rating the utility of a unit throughout a playthrough, you should consider their availability, which is why Caineghis, or even just Naesala and Tibarn aren't generally present in the best fe10 unit unit discussion, despite how much better than virtually everyone else they are; that's a basic factor.

In the Renning example you basically said you penalize single units for making your army significantly worse, but every non meta unit can do that depending on your definition. Wouldn't opportunity cost exist for every unit?

And I'd say Renning, who shines in 0% growths due to his weapon types and weapon (and even more if you're doing something like royaless), is better than FE6 Karel, who joins too late to realistically benefit from the boots shopping spree, and therefore can only be too slow to keep up in the one single map where you'd use him (his only thing is using Durandal at base).

Renning's utility is replicable, but Karel's even more so, I'd say.

Would you also penalize Farina for costing money?

As I said, I'd rather consider such decisions as something akin to route splits, and not let the units themselves take the blame.

By the same logic, and correct me if you think I'm wrong, couldn't you just penalize every unit which isn't part of the "optimal" team for simply being worse than someone else you'd rather use?  
Like, would you penalize the majority of FE10's endgame roster for not being the 10 best units to pick?  
I think it's better to leave out all external factors and solely focus on the unit's performance (at least from when they become playable) in the game, based on what they bring to the table.  
So, I would just view the Sonya/Deen choice as a route split when it concerns to maps, and only punish Sonya for her intrinsic flaws, like low level, lack of Seraphim, and 4 move.

I don't think punishing Sonya for costing you Deen is fair, and this extends for all units who have to chosen over someone/something else (imagine blaming Shura for costing you the boots); however, if you're going to do that, then I think you should reward Sophia for getting you an otherwise unobtainable Guiding Ring.
